1. On the issue page, `listMembers` supplies the composer with member records joined to their user records. In [mention-query.ts](src/components/domain/comment/mention-query.ts), `mentionHandle` defines a handle as the lowercased part of the member’s email before `@`. The autocomplete can insert that handle, but someone can type it directly too.

2. As the body changes, [mention-textarea.tsx](src/components/domain/comment/mention-textarea.tsx) calls `resolveMentions` from [mentions.ts](src/lib/mentions.ts). That function extracts handles from the body and maps each one to a matching member’s `userId`; repeated mentions are deduplicated, and unknown handles are dropped. Code spans and fenced code blocks are ignored. The textarea passes both the body and resolved IDs to [comment-composer.tsx](src/components/domain/comment/comment-composer.tsx), which validates them with `createCommentSchema` and submits `mentionedUserIds` alongside the body.

3. The server action [create-comment.ts](src/actions/comments/create-comment.ts) validates and authorizes the request, then calls `createComment` in [comment-service.ts](src/server/services/comment-service.ts). The service resolves mentions again against up to 100 organization members. It uses the IDs parsed from the body plus any client-provided IDs that belong to those members, then saves the resulting list on the comment and emits `comment.created` with the same `mentionedUserIds`. The event type is defined in [event.ts](src/types/event.ts).

4. [instrumentation.ts](src/instrumentation.ts) loads [event-registry.ts](src/server/services/event-registry.ts) when the server starts. Importing the registry loads [notification-service.ts](src/server/services/notification-service.ts), whose `registerFanOut` subscribes to `comment.created`. Its handler calls `notify` for the mentioned IDs using kind `comment_mention`; `notify` deduplicates recipients, skips the comment author, looks up each recipient’s preference for that kind, resolves the channels, and inserts a notification row if any channel remains. [notification-repository.ts](src/server/repositories/notification-repository.ts) writes the row, including its `channels`, to the database.

5. For a missing preference, `notify` defaults to `in_app` and `email`. With a saved preference, `resolveChannels` uses `inApp` and `email`; `digestOnly` affects whether the email channel is allowed when the organization’s `digest_email` flag is enabled. That flag is plan-gated in [config/feature-flags.ts](src/config/feature-flags.ts). If both channels resolve to empty, `notify` skips the row. Otherwise it inserts a row even when its only channel is `email`. The inbox page reads notification rows without filtering by `channels`, so an email-only row can still appear there.

There’s an important distinction between a channel being recorded and an email being sent: this comment-mention path does not send an immediate mention email. Although a mention template exists in `src/emails/mention-email.tsx` and is registered by `src/emails/render.ts`, no mention fan-out calls it. The digest path in [digest-service.ts](src/server/services/digest-service.ts) and [digest-email-job.ts](src/server/jobs/digest-email-job.ts) can send a daily digest for recipients with a `digestOnly` preference and unread notifications; its query does not filter by notification kind or channels. Also, `sendEmail` in [email-service.ts](src/server/services/email-service.ts) logs the email draft rather than sending it through an outbound mail service.
